clue.text: Lobby for charm

definitions.meaning: a lobby is the hall or doorway area you come in through
to charm is to enchant or delight someone, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a hotel lobby for its charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are senses of one spelling: a front hall, and a verb meaning to put someone in a trance of delight.

clue.text: Murderer, one in jail

indicators.note: in places the word for one inside the word for jail

parts.note: can is slang for a prison
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A killer serving time, one inmate among many.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son kills his brother Abel, the first murderer in the Bible.

clue.text: Marriage guidance service for clergymen getting their ends away

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the clergymen word are removed, with a cheeky slang double meaning

parts.note: prelates are senior clergymen such as bishops

explanation.surface: A counselling service for vicars whose marriages are in trouble after illicit affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting their ends away' is British slang for having sex, which makes the surface naughty; mechanically it strips P and S from PRELATES. RELATE is a British relationship-counselling charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Relate is the name of the UK charity offering couples counselling, formerly the Marriage Guidance Council.

clue.text: Losing time over faulty electronic compass

indicators.note: losing says some letters go missing from the fodder
faulty means the remaining letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A broken electronic compass that keeps losing time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T and O from ELECTRONIC and rearrange the rest. 'Compass' is a verb here, meaning to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To compass something, in the old literary sense, is to go round it or surround it on all sides.

clue.text: Atoms in motion acquiring pressure in this place?

definitions.text: Atoms in motion acquiring pressure in this place?

indicators.note: letters in motion are moving around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
this place means here

explanation.surface: A physics question about the gas all around us.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the air we live in is moving atoms that exert pressure right here.
explanation.definitionFit: The air surrounding the earth is a mass of moving gas molecules that exerts pressure on everything around us.

clue.text: Primarily, they hurt badly with original saying?

definitions.text: Primarily, they hurt badly with original saying?

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the next word
badly says the letters of they's opening plus hurt are jumbled

parts.note: the original, or first, letter of the word saying is S

explanation.surface: A musing that home truths sting most when they are freshly said.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a description of the answer: honest statements that hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts plainly stated are often painful to hear, as the saying about home truths suggests.

clue.text: Presiding officers trading power for new shoes?

indicators.note: the letter for power is swapped out for the letter for new

parts.note: a Speaker presides over a parliamentary chamber

explanation.surface: Parliamentary chairmen swapping their authority for a fresh pair of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: P (power) in SPEAKERS becomes N (new). The question mark flags that soft shoes are merely one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-soled trainers are called this in American usage, so they are one kind of footwear.

clue.text: Dark forces clued around this grid

parts.note: kept in the dark means kept hidden, unknown
agents are the forces or powers that bring something about

explanation.surface: Sinister powers hinted at all through the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Many answers in the grid are spies or spying words (informants, sneakers, Svengali's control), and the setter hid a further message around the edge of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's theme: spies and spying turn up in clues and answers throughout this grid.

clue.text: Character brewing tea with urn

indicators.note: brewing, like a pot of tea, stirs the letters together into a new order

explanation.surface: A homely scene of tea made in an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's inborn temperament is their character, their basic makeup.

clue.text: King's playable after one club

indicators.note: after puts the king and playable pieces behind the one piece

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
a shot or plan that is on is possible or playable

explanation.surface: A card game: the king can be played after the first club.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is card play, but the club is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's bag holds several metal-headed clubs numbered by loft, each called by this name.

clue.text: They say Gemmill leaps over fancy formations

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are heard, not written

parts.note: Archie Gemmill was a Scotland footballer; leaps are vaults

explanation.surface: Football talk: Gemmill hurdling defenders in a showy dribble.
explanation.walkthrough: Archie Gemmill scored a famous dribbled goal for Scotland in the 1978 World Cup. ARCHIE VAULTS, said out loud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are ornamental mouldings running around the curve of an arch, decorative architectural features.

clue.text: In Paris one time with regret? Not so

parts.note: un is French for one
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A wistful question about a time in Paris one regrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not so means it is false or inaccurate.

clue.text: Close lorry wrecked car

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A lorry passing close by wrecks a car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous British luxury motor-car marque.

clue.text: Space travel is male fantasy

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Space travel is a typical men's daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreating into daydreams to avoid reality is a kind of fantasy.

clue.text: Go away and don't come back!

definitions.text: Go away and don't come back!

parts.words: Go away and don't come back!
parts.note: a rude dismissal, read cryptically as an order to lose one's way so one cannot return

explanation.surface: An angry dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt slang order telling someone to leave, and literally becoming unable to find the way home.

clue.text: Manage risk getting married? His indefinite engagement

indicators.note: manage here means to handle and rearrange the letters of risk
indefinite means not fixed, so the letters of his are not in fixed order

explanation.surface: Wedding advice: marriage is a risk, an engagement of uncertain length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests betrothal next to 'married', but it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief minor clash of troops is a military engagement.

clue.text: Minister's language is spin

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, title of a minister
Erse is Irish or Scots Gaelic

explanation.surface: A preacher's talk is just political spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests government spin; here spin means to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin a car round is to turn it about, putting it into the opposite direction.

clue.text: Ketamine for breakfast?

definitions.meaning: street slang name for the drug ketamine

explanation.surface: A startling question about drugs at the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: Kellogg's cereal brand shares its name with the street nickname for the anaesthetic drug.

clue.text: See 8
Saving for the future, as things might go wrong

indicators.note: letters that go wrong fall out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting money aside, since things might go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding away a store of something for later use is saving it.

clue.text: It's meant to be cycled around Germany

definitions.text: It's meant to be cycled around Germany

indicators.note: around places the scrambled letters on both sides of the Germany letter
cycled means the letters of meant are spun round into a new order

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A bicycle built for two, ridden on a German tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be cycled' rearranges MEANT to TANEM, which goes around D. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater bicycle is made to be ridden, and could well be ridden around Germany.

clue.text: Country joined Europe to mine tin

indicators.note: to mine is to dig into, so the other pieces go inside the tin letters

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
to wed is to join in marriage

explanation.surface: A nation joining the EU so it can dig for tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian kingdom, so a country.

clue.text: Group of tsetse flies

indicators.note: flies is read as a verb, the letters of tsetse flying apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A swarm of tsetse flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like the noun after tsetse, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of six, such as six singers or six lines of a sonnet, is a group.

clue.text: Canaries playing well as Norwich team score headers

parts.note: a player in form is playing well

indicators.note: headers, a football word, here means the head letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Norwich City, nicknamed the Canaries, in good form scoring headed goals.
explanation.walkthrough: Norwich City FC are known as the Canaries; but a canary is also slang for someone who sings to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Underworld slang calls a police informer a canary, because they sing.

clue.text: Bad back during delivery

indicators.note: back says the letters found are read in reverse
during says the letters sit inside the word delivery

explanation.surface: A backache suffered while giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' finds LIVE inside 'delivery', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked or morally wrong is bad.

clue.text: Border guard wants heroin

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the heroin letter is removed

parts.note: to hedge is to guard or protect, as in hedging a bet
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A frontier guard looking for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of something is its border or rim.

clue.text: The devil's cards?

parts.note: deuce is an old word for the devil, and in cards it is a two

explanation.surface: Playing cards owned by Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Twos in a pack of cards share their name with an old euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: When Vangelis composed, he was hypnotically in control

indicators.note: composed, a nod to the composer Vangelis, means the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: The composer Vangelis held his audience spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: In du Maurier's novel Trilby, the sinister musician mesmerises and dominates a young singer.
